draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Agonda! This 3 km stretch of sand is one of only four beaches in the country designated as a turtle nesting site under the 2011 coastal rules. Olive ridley turtles come ashore here to nest, so the whole place stays wonderfully quiet.
draft.hungryLine: Agonda keeps it simple, think fish thalis at a local joint and fresh juices at a family-run cafe.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Pop into St. Anne Church, it's just a minute's walk, then go have a look at the abandoned Sina Hotel that locals call the Ghost Hotel.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Just stay on the beach. It's simple and natural, and when the officials clear away the stray sunbeds it looks even better.
moodReplies.surprise-me: In 2016 TripAdvisor's Travelers' Choice ranked Agonda Beach fourth in Asia and first in India.

spots.name: St. Anne Church
spots.detail: 1 min walk · The village church, right by the beach road

spots.name: Sina Hotel
spots.detail: In Agonda · A half-built five-star hotel, abandoned since the early 1990s

spots.name: Cabo de Rama
spots.detail: Short drive · Ruined fort named for Lord Rama, with a Portuguese-era chapel still in use

legends.title: The Ghost Hotel
legends.body: Locals call the abandoned Sina Hotel the Ghost Hotel. Building stopped in the early 1990s, and the story got darker when one of its owners was murdered.

tips.title: Keep it dark at night.
tips.body: Turtles nest on this beach, so keep noise and lights down after dark to give them a chance.

tips.title: Expect a quiet low season.
tips.body: Most eateries open only in high season, though Dersey's at the south end stays open through the low season too.

story.title: A king's fort
story.body: Up the coast, a Hindu king built the fort of Cabo de Rama, named for Lord Rama. After a few battles it was taken over by the Portuguese.

story.title: The hotel that never opened
story.body: A group of Russians set out to build a five-star hotel in Agonda. Money ran out, legal trouble piled up and the structure was left to decay.

story.title: A beach for turtles
story.body: The Coastal Regulation Zone notification of 2011 named Agonda one of only four turtle nesting beaches. Olive ridleys nest here, with September mentioned as a nesting month.

story.title: Quiet on purpose
story.body: Agonda is a village of about 3,800 people that has stayed calm and natural. Yoga schools and a winter meditation ashram draw a gentle crowd.

food.name: Dersey's
food.detail: Indian and local food at the south end of the beach

food.name: Blue Planet Cafe
food.detail: Family-run organic vegetarian and vegan cafe, go for the juices, smoothies and vegan cakes
